obs: "The repeal of the act of 1848 could not, upon any sound principle of law, revive any previous act which was repugnant to the provisions contained in the repealing act of 1849."
"the Revised Statutes provide in express terms that, whenever an act is repealed which repealed a former act, such former act shall not thereby be revived unless it shall be expressly so provided."
Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul Railway Co. v. United States
"and 12 of the Revised Statutes provides that the repeal of a repealing statute shall not revive the original act."
Merchants' Cotton Press & Storage Co. v. Insurance Co. of North America

"it is settled by King v. Cornell, 106 U.S. 395, that subdivision two of section 639 of the Revised Statutes was repealed by the act of 1875, ... and this subdivision two of that section was not restored by the act of March 3, 1887"

"Nor do we perceive any ground for imputing the intention to Congress to revive the Captured and Abandoned Property Act for the purposes of this action. This is not the case of the revival of a law by express renactment, or by the repeal of a repealing clause; and if such had been the intention of Congress, no reason suggests itself why Congress should not have unequivocally said so."
